original_test_intent: Verify that supported settings on the BIOS Socket Configuration > Processor Configuration page can be changed to approved non-default values, persist across a save/reboot, and return to the authoritative platform defaults after Load Defaults, with correct CPU/socket topology and no new firmware, POST, BMC or OS errors.
original_method: Record motherboard/CPU/socket population, BIOS build, setup page and complete default-value oracle; preserve existing logs rather than clearing them; use local/remote KVM under maintenance approval to change one qualified reversible setting at a time according to a dependency-aware matrix; capture before/change/save/retained states and boot milestones; invoke the approved Load Defaults action, save/reboot and re-enter the same page; compare every scoped value to SPEC and verify CPU enumeration, POST and logs; stop at first no-boot/topology fault and recover through the approved BIOS/CMOS mechanism without blind retry.
manual_activity: A qualified operator controls the BIOS setup through a physical console or approved KVM, changes only the authorized Processor Configuration values, performs each save/reboot, captures page/POST evidence and executes Load Defaults and recovery if required.
required_inputs: Motherboard/CPU/socket population, BIOS/BMC/ME/microcode versions and exact Processor Configuration page path
Revision-controlled SPEC defaults and a dependency-aware matrix of supported reversible non-default values
KVM/console, maintenance window, boot/readiness deadlines, active-workload clearance and evidence plan
Known-good settings, BIOS recovery/clear-CMOS ownership, physical access and stop/recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Never execute `all/random setting`; approve each value, dependency, expected effect and restoration before save
Preserve existing SEL/kernel/system logs and establish timestamps/markers instead of clearing evidence
Change one controlled setting or approved dependency group at a time and retain the last-known-good screenshot
Verify CPU/socket/core/thread/NUMA/topology and POST after each reboot; stop on mismatch, hang, crash or error delta
Do not automate reboot loops or clear CMOS; recovery is qualified-personnel controlled with no automatic retry
agent_execution_scope: Validate hardware/firmware identity, default oracle, safe setting matrix, dependencies, maintenance and recovery
Guide the operator through documented checkpoints and collect complete screenshots, boot timing, CPU topology and pre/post log deltas
Compare persistence and post-Load-Defaults values to the exact SPEC without declaring hardware PASS
Do not navigate BIOS autonomously, choose random values, clear logs, save unapproved settings, reboot blindly or invoke CMOS recovery
engineer_actions: Approve the exact Processor Configuration page, SPEC defaults and safe reversible value/dependency matrix
Approve reboot/readiness/error criteria, log-preservation method, KVM/physical recovery and stop conditions
Review screenshots, retention/default, topology and log evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.command_recommendation: Qualified operator follows the approved Processor Configuration matrix through KVM, saving/rebooting for persistence and Load Defaults restoration while the agent organizes non-destructive identity/topology/log evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Processor Configuration page, persistence/default-restore sequence and 5/20-minute allocation remain; the unsafe all/random scope is constrained to an owner-approved matrix rather than silently executed.

modernized_recommendation.status: HIGH MANUAL PROCESSOR-CONFIGURATION PERSISTENCE AND DEFAULT-RESTORE TEST
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a revision-controlled one-setting-at-a-time matrix with screenshots at baseline, changed, retained and restored states, plus CPU topology and error-log deltas after each reboot.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces arbitrary changes and destructive log clearing with safe coverage selection, dependency control, preserved evidence and recoverable checkpoints.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A single arbitrary value may miss dependent settings, while changing all values together makes failures untraceable and can prevent boot before evidence is collected.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Processor configuration can disable cores/threads/features, alter NUMA or power behavior, change socket enumeration and cause POST failure or no-boot.

project_override_considerations: If KVM macro automation exists, it remains operator-supervised manual execution unless separately validated to identify page/build, confirm every screen and stop safely. Load Defaults may affect unrelated BIOS domains, so the owner must define snapshot and restoration scope.
expected_evidence: Exact row/variant/hash, approval and motherboard/CPU/socket/BIOS identity
SPEC default matrix, selected non-default values, dependencies and last-known-good recovery plan
Timestamped baseline, changed, saved, retained, Load-Defaults and restored BIOS screenshots
POST/boot readiness, CPU/socket/core/thread/NUMA enumeration after each phase
Preserved pre/post BMC/SEL/kernel/system error evidence with no unexplained deltas

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently define Processor Configuration change/persistence/default restoration. `All/random` is unsafe and underspecified but does not conflict with the stated acceptance; it is constrained by the review without altering Master.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The manual BIOS workflow is clear. A safe matrix, exact defaults, operator and recovery plan are supplyable prerequisites.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2176 Wistron-BIOS-00493-V004: approve motherboard/CPU/socket/BIOS identity, exact Processor Configuration page and full SPEC defaults; safe reversible non-default values, dependencies and coverage replacing `all/random`; reboot/readiness/topology/error criteria, log-preservation approach, Load-Defaults blast radius, stop conditions, KVM/physical recovery, and clear-CMOS ownership.

review_improvement: Makes the Processor Configuration test traceable and recoverable while preserving persistence/default coverage and preventing arbitrary settings or log destruction from masking a no-boot cause.
independent_technical_reasoning: Processor Configuration settings can interact and materially change visible CPU topology. Changing all or random values at once cannot isolate failures and can remove the very management/boot path needed to recover. The evidence must therefore be page- and build-specific, use approved reversible values, and correlate each reboot with CPU enumeration and log deltas. The core act remains manual because pre-OS navigation and visual confirmation cannot be trusted to SSH-only automation.
